articles.title: KSRTC FlyBus Staff Brutally Assaulted on Bengaluru–Mysuru Highway
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Concerns over the safety of commuters and public transport staff on the Bengaluru–Mysuru Expressway have intensified after a KSRTC FlyBus driver and conductor were allegedly assaulted by a group of men in Mandya. Police have arrested two accused in connection with the incident.

body.html:
Concerns over the safety of commuters and public transport staff on the Bengaluru–Mysuru Expressway have intensified after a KSRTC FlyBus driver and conductor were allegedly assaulted by a group of men in Mandya. Police have arrested two accused in connection with the incident.

The incident occurred in the early hours of July 5 near the underpass at Induvalu village on the Bengaluru–Mysuru Access Way. The FlyBus was travelling from Kempegowda International Airport to Mysuru and had briefly stopped in Mandya to allow passengers to alight.

According to police, while proceeding along the service road, the bus was intercepted by a group of men allegedly travelling against the designated one-way. When driver Vinod and conductor Eranna questioned them, the men allegedly abused the KSRTC staff, claimed they were "Mandya locals" and continued creating trouble despite being warned that the police would be informed.

The accused allegedly assaulted the driver and conductor, leaving both injured. They were later shifted to a hospital, where they received treatment.

The attack was captured on video and widely circulated on social media, triggering public outrage and renewed concerns over law and order on the Bengaluru–Mysuru Expressway and its service roads.

Based on a complaint, Mandya Rural Police registered an FIR under Crime No. 326/2026 under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), including Sections 115(2), 126(2), 132, 190 and 352.

Police arrested 24-year-old Varun and detained a 17-year-old juvenile in connection with the case. Efforts are underway to identify and trace the remaining accused.

The incident comes days after another road rage attack near Maddur, where a Bengaluru man was allegedly dragged out of his car and assaulted in front of his family, raising fresh concerns over the safety of motorists and public transport employees on one of Karnataka's busiest highway corridors.

#Karnataka #Mandya #KSRTC #FlyBus #RoadRage

articles.title: ‘Help, Kidnapper!’ Child's Cries Trigger Massive Police Hunt, Truth Leaves Everyone Stunned
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A child's repeated cries of "Help, help, kidnapper!" late on Tuesday triggered panic among passersby and a massive police search in Uttar Pradesh's Gorakhpur district. Hours later, police discovered there had been no kidnapping.

body.html:
A child's repeated cries of "Help, help, kidnapper!" late on Tuesday triggered panic among passersby and a massive police search in Uttar Pradesh's Gorakhpur district. Hours later, police discovered there had been no kidnapping.

The alarm was raised around 10 pm after people heard the child shouting for help while travelling on a motorcycle. Believing he was being abducted, they alerted the police.

Teams from Shahpur and Chiluatal police stations rushed to the spot. Police examined CCTV footage, questioned local residents and launched a search for the suspected kidnappers.

After tracing those involved, investigators found that the child had been staying at his maternal grandmother's house for the past few days. On Tuesday night, his mother and maternal uncle were taking him back home on a motorcycle when he began shouting, "Help... Kidnapper!"

Police separately questioned the child, his mother and his maternal uncle, and videographed the inquiry.

The investigation revealed that the boy did not want to return home. According to police, he wanted to continue staying with his grandmother and was also unwilling to resume his studies.

Investigators said the child deliberately raised the alarm, hoping passersby would intervene and send him back to his grandmother's house.

After examining CCTV footage and questioning those involved, police confirmed within about an hour that no kidnapping or any other criminal offence had taken place.

Although no criminal case was registered, the child's cries prompted a full-scale police response and briefly led residents to believe that a kidnapping was underway.

#UttarPradesh #Gorakhpur #ViralNews #Police #BreakingNews

articles.title: Pedestrian Killed at Vijayawada PNBS, Police Probe Driver and Victim's Role
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A tragic accident at the Pandit Nehru Bus Station (PNBS) in Vijayawada claimed the life of a pedestrian on Wednesday, with police investigating whether driver negligence, pedestrian distraction, or both led to the fatal mishap.

body.html:
A tragic accident at the Pandit Nehru Bus Station (PNBS) in Vijayawada claimed the life of a pedestrian on Wednesday, with police investigating whether driver negligence, pedestrian distraction, or both led to the fatal mishap.

The deceased has been identified as Balu Sahu, a native of Odisha.

According to police, Sahu was walking from the arrival block towards the city bus terminal when he was hit by an APSRTC bus. He died on the spot due to the impact.

Preliminary investigations suggest that Sahu was looking at his mobile phone while crossing the busy bus station premises at the time of the accident.

Police also suspect that the APSRTC bus driver, attached to the Avanigadda depot, was driving at an excessive speed despite heavy passenger movement inside the terminal.

The entire incident was captured on CCTV cameras installed at the bus station. Investigators are examining the footage to determine the exact sequence of events and whether the accident was primarily caused by driver negligence, pedestrian inattention, or a combination of both.

Krishnalanka Police have registered a case, and further investigation is underway.

The incident has once again raised concerns over pedestrian safety and vehicle speed regulation within the crowded PNBS premises, where thousands of passengers move between platforms every day.

#AndhraPradesh #Vijayawada #RoadAccident #PNBS #BreakingNews

articles.title: Kerala MBBS Student Found Dead in Uzbekistan: Classmate Arrested, Family Alleges Brutal Assault
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A 21-year-old Kerala medical student was allegedly murdered by her classmate in Uzbekistan, with her family claiming she was brutally assaulted and pressured to convert her religion before her death.

body.html:
A 21-year-old Kerala medical student was allegedly murdered by her classmate in Uzbekistan, with her family claiming she was brutally assaulted and pressured to convert her religion before her death.

The victim, Sawariya Basanth, a native of Haripad in Alappuzha district, was a first-year MBBS student at Bukhara State Medical Institute. The accused, 23-year-old Sadarul Anam, a native of Malappuram, has been arrested by Uzbek authorities.

According to investigators, the incident took place on Friday following an altercation between the two students. Police alleged that Anam struck Sawariya on the head with a laptop during the argument. She collapsed unconscious and was taken to a hospital by the accused, where she was declared dead. Uzbek authorities arrested Anam the same day and launched an investigation.

However, Sawariya's family has disputed the claim that the laptop injury alone caused her death. Her relatives alleged that her body bore multiple injuries from head to toe, indicating that she had been brutally assaulted.

Janeesh, Sawariya's maternal uncle, who travelled to Uzbekistan to bring back her body, alleged that the accused had been pressuring her to convert her religion and that she had repeatedly refused.

"Fellow students informed me about the attempts at religious conversion. The attack was not an immediate provocation. She suffered brutal injuries from her legs to her head. We therefore decided to conduct a second postmortem to uncover the truth," he alleged.

Sawariya had travelled to Uzbekistan in December last year to pursue her MBBS. According to her family, she had performed well academically and had completed her first semester with good results.

After her body was brought to Kerala, a second postmortem was conducted at Alappuzha Medical College. Her father, Basanth, who works in Kuwait, filed a complaint with the Alappuzha District Police Chief seeking a detailed investigation into the circumstances surrounding her death.

Based on the complaint, Haripad Police registered a case against Sadarul Anam, who remains in police custody in Uzbekistan. Police said the investigation has begun and they are awaiting the postmortem report.

Officials said the accused is currently in Uzbek police custody and that the necessary legal procedures will be followed to bring him back to India if required.

#Kerala #Uzbekistan #CrimeNews #MBBSStudent #Alappuzha

articles.title: Woman Forced to Remove Veil, Man Made to Apply Sindoor on Road; Viral Video Leads to Arrests
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A woman was allegedly harassed by a group of men while travelling on a motorcycle with her male friend in Bihar's Nawada district. The group allegedly forced her to remove her face veil and compelled the man accompanying her to apply sindoor (vermilion) on her forehead.

body.html:
A woman was allegedly harassed by a group of men while travelling on a motorcycle with her male friend in Bihar's Nawada district. The group allegedly forced her to remove her face veil and compelled the man accompanying her to apply sindoor (vermilion) on her forehead.

A video of the incident, which went viral on social media, led to the registration of an FIR and the arrest of several accused.

According to videos circulating online, the woman repeatedly pleaded with the group to stop harassing her as they filmed the incident on their mobile phones. Despite her appeals, the men allegedly removed her face veil while recording the encounter. Religious slogans could also be heard in the background.

The man travelling with the woman also requested the group to let them go. However, the group allegedly insisted that he apply sindoor on the woman's forehead. The pair were reportedly followed for some distance while the group continued recording videos.

The viral footage triggered widespread reactions on social media, with several users claiming that the incident involved individuals from different religious communities. However, Nawada Police said these claims were false and that the incident was being given a misleading communal narrative online.

Police said they immediately launched an investigation after the video surfaced. Using the motorcycle's registration details, investigators traced the vehicle to its previous owner and subsequently identified and questioned the man and woman seen in the video.

According to police, the investigation found that both individuals belong to the same community and have known each other for a considerable period. They were travelling together with mutual consent when they were allegedly intercepted and harassed by a group of anti-social elements.

Police have registered a criminal case, identified several accused and taken them into custody. Efforts are underway to identify and arrest the remaining individuals involved. Investigators are examining the viral videos, witness statements and other digital evidence, and further legal action will be taken based on the findings of the investigation.

#Bihar #Nawada #ViralVideo #CrimeNews #PoliceInvestigation

articles.title: Student Assaults Principal After Being Caught, Teachers Stage Protest
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Tension prevailed at the Government Degree College in Bhainsa town of Telangana's Nirmal district after a candidate appearing for an examination allegedly assaulted the college principal when confronted over suspected malpractice.

body.html:
Tension prevailed at the Government Degree College in Bhainsa town of Telangana's Nirmal district after a candidate appearing for an examination allegedly assaulted the college principal when confronted over suspected malpractice.

The incident triggered protests by the college's teaching staff, with lecturers wearing black badges to condemn the alleged attack and demanding strict action against the accused. The protesting staff also called for stronger measures to ensure the safety of teaching staff in educational institutions.

According to college officials, Ganga Srikanth was appearing for the second-semester examination of Dr BR Ambedkar Open University when he was allegedly found copying during the examination.

Principal K Buchaiah reportedly questioned him over the alleged malpractice. Officials alleged that the candidate reacted aggressively, pushed the principal and assaulted an invigilator and other members of the college staff. During the altercation, he also allegedly tore up his own answer sheet.

Following the incident, Principal Buchaiah lodged a complaint with the local police, seeking legal action against the accused. Police have launched an investigation into the matter.

The incident has renewed concerns over the safety of educators and the need for stricter enforcement of examination rules, with college staff demanding immediate action against the accused.

#Telangana #Nirmal #ExamMalpractice #College #BreakingNews

articles.title: Love Marriage Ends in Tragedy: BDO, Woman SI Arrested as Videos Surface in Alleged Dowry Murder Case
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: What began as a friendship between two civil services aspirants and culminated in a love marriage has ended in a case of alleged dowry death, murder and an alleged extramarital relationship, police said.

body.html:
What began as a friendship between two civil services aspirants and culminated in a love marriage has ended in a case of alleged dowry death, murder and an alleged extramarital relationship, police said.

Police on Wednesday arrested Begusarai woman Sub-Inspector (SI) Annu Kumari in connection with the death of 29-year-old Amrita Kumari, wife of Jale Block Development Officer (BDO) Manoj Kumar. The arrest came a day after Manoj Kumar was arrested from the border area of Muzaffarpur and Darbhanga districts.

According to police, Annu Kumari, who is suspected to have been in a relationship with Manoj Kumar, was arrested from her native village in Sursand, Sitamarhi district. Investigators are probing her alleged role in the case.

Police said Manoj and Amrita first met in 2015 while preparing for the Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC) examination. Their friendship developed into a relationship. Manoj was selected as an auditor in the Ministry of Defence in 2018, and the couple entered into a court marriage in 2020. After Manoj was selected as a BDO in 2022, they solemnised their marriage with the consent of both families in 2023.

According to the investigation, the relationship later turned strained after Manoj allegedly became involved with Annu Kumari. Police said the alleged affair frequently led to domestic disputes, and Amrita allegedly faced continuous mental and physical harassment after objecting to the relationship.

Amrita was found unconscious at her residence in Kanhauli under the Mithanpura police station limits in Muzaffarpur on the night of July 4. She was initially admitted to a private hospital and later shifted to another hospital after her condition deteriorated, but she died on the way.

Following her death, Amrita's brother, Rajkumar, lodged an FIR at Mithanpura Police Station on July 5, alleging that Manoj Kumar murdered his wife because of his alleged relationship with the woman SI.

The FIR alleges that about a year after the marriage, Manoj, along with his parents, brother and sister, began demanding ₹10 lakh as dowry. When the demand was not met, Amrita was allegedly subjected to continuous harassment. The complaint further alleges that after Amrita opposed her husband's alleged affair, the harassment intensified and that she was administered an intoxicating substance on the night of July 3 before being murdered.

Apart from Manoj Kumar, his parents, brother and sister have also been named as accused in the case.

Meanwhile, two videos showing Amrita allegedly being assaulted have surfaced on social media. Her family claims the videos were recorded at the BDO's official residence in Kanhauli and are from March 19, 2025. They allege the footage shows Amrita being dragged on the stairs, assaulted by her in-laws and forcibly pushed into a vehicle marked "District Administration." The family has submitted the videos to the police as evidence.

Mithanpura SHO Ajay Kumar said police have seized two mobile phones from Manoj Kumar, and their call detail records (CDR) and other digital evidence are being examined. CCTV footage, forensic evidence and the post-mortem report are also being analysed.

Police said the investigation is focused on the alleged dowry demand, the alleged extramarital relationship and the circumstances surrounding Amrita Kumari's death. Further legal action will be taken based on the evidence collected.

#Bihar #Muzaffarpur #DowryDeath #BDO #CrimeNews

articles.title: UP Constable's Abuse of Fruit Vendor Caught on Camera, Probe Ordered
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A video from the Jali Kothi area under the Delhi Gate Police Station limits in Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, has surfaced on social media, showing a police constable allegedly abusing a fruit vendor.

body.html:
A video from the Jali Kothi area under the Delhi Gate Police Station limits in Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, has surfaced on social media, showing a police constable allegedly abusing a fruit vendor. Following the viral video, Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Avinash Pandey has ordered an inquiry into the incident.

In the video, constable Gajendra Sharma is allegedly heard telling the fruit vendor, "I will defecate in your mouth." When a young man attempted to record the incident, the constable allegedly struck his mobile phone, causing it to fall. The incident was also recorded by other people present at the scene.

The fruit vendor alleged that the constable approached his cart without any provocation and began verbally abusing him. When he objected, an argument broke out, and several local residents expressed their displeasure over the constable's behaviour.

Some local residents claimed that the constable appeared to be under the influence of alcohol at the time of the incident. However, this allegation has not been officially confirmed, and no medical examination report has been released.

Taking cognisance of the viral video, SSP Avinash Pandey ordered an inquiry against constable Gajendra Sharma. The investigation has been assigned to the Circle Officer (CO), Kotwali.

#UttarPradesh #Meerut #UPPolice #ViralVideo #PoliceMisconduct

articles.title: Thousands of LPG Cylinders Swept Away in Floods, Shocking River Scene Triggers Safety Alert
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking incident has emerged from Maharashtra's Raigad district, where around 3,000 LPG cylinders were swept away by floodwaters from the HPCL Patalganga LPG Bottling Plant following heavy rainfall.

body.html:
A shocking incident has emerged from Maharashtra's Raigad district, where around 3,000 LPG cylinders were swept away by floodwaters from the HPCL Patalganga LPG Bottling Plant following heavy rainfall.

According to officials, torrential rain caused the plant's protective wall to collapse, allowing floodwaters to enter the premises and wash away both filled and empty LPG cylinders into the Patalganga River and Kharpada Creek. Videos showed hundreds of cylinders floating downstream as startled residents recorded the scene from a nearby bridge.

The administration said some of the cylinders may still be filled with LPG, posing a serious safety risk.

Raigad Collector Kishan Jawale has appealed to the public not to pick up, open or take home any cylinders found in or around the river.

"There is no guarantee whether the cylinders washed into the river contain gas or whether they are in a safe condition. Picking them up, opening them or taking them home out of curiosity or for use could be extremely dangerous," the collector said.

Residents have been asked to hand over any recovered cylinders to the HPCL Patalganga LPG Bottling Plant, any nearby HPCL dealer, the Tehsildar Offices at Khalapur or Panvel, or the office of the Sub-Divisional Officer (SDO).

Officials are assessing the situation and efforts are underway to trace and recover the cylinders washed away by the floodwaters.

Continuous heavy rain has caused widespread flooding across several parts of Maharashtra over the past week, with Raigad among the worst-affected districts.

#Maharashtra #Raigad #Floods #LPGCylinder #BreakingNews

articles.title: Family Chased on Highway, Accused Arrested After Attack Caught on Dashcam
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: The Maddur Town Police have arrested seven members for allegedly attacking a Bengaluru family following a road rage incident on the Bengaluru-Mysuru Highway.

body.html:
The Maddur Town Police have arrested seven members for allegedly attacking a Bengaluru family following a road rage incident on the Bengaluru-Mysuru Highway.

The incident took place on the night of July 5 when Sagar Kumar (37), an assistant manager at BMRCL, was travelling with his family from Mysuru to Bengaluru. According to police, the confrontation began after his car allegedly brushed against another vehicle near the Srirangapatna toll plaza.

Police said both parties initially resolved the matter and continued their journey. However, after inspecting the damage to their vehicle, the accused allegedly chased Sagar's car in two vehicles up to Maddur.

The gang allegedly intercepted Sagar's car in the middle of the highway and dragged him out before brutally assaulting him. They also allegedly attacked his mother, wife and eight-year-old child. Dashcam footage of the assault, which later went viral on social media, showed the attackers kicking and punching Sagar in front of his family. One of the accused was also seen striking him with what appeared to be a metal object.

Sagar's wife stepped out of the vehicle and pleaded with the attackers to stop before passing motorists intervened and dispersed the group.

After receiving information, Maddur Town Police rescued the family. Sagar, who was undergoing treatment at the Mandya Institute of Medical Sciences, has since returned to Bengaluru with his family.

Police initially arrested Santosh, Arun Kumar and Abhishek in connection with the case. On Wednesday morning, two more accused, Venkate Gowda and Pratap, were arrested in Bengaluru.

Police have seized two vehicles allegedly used in the crime. A case has been registered under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for assault, criminal intimidation and acts endangering life. Further investigation is underway.

#Karnataka #Mandya #RoadRage #BengaluruMysuruExpressway #BreakingNews
